question: Caught between the aviation sector’s rhetoric, which claims that the EU’s environmental regulation imposed an additional EUR 15 billion in costs on air transport in 2024 – a figure expected to double by 20301 – and the Commission’s scrutiny on mergers and possible abusive practices in the sector, EU passengers continue to face very high airfares2. The EU also seems to lead the global delay ranking.

One in three air passengers in the EU has been affected by delays and flight cancellations3. Meanwhile, the European Parliament is working on a revision of the common rules on compensation and assistance for passengers and an amendment of Regulation (EC) No 2027/97 on air carrier liability. In this context, could the Commission clarify: 1.
The outcome of its 20234 investigations into high flight prices and whether it is considering a study on unfair commercial practices (UCP) in aviation, particularly cartel behaviour.
If it can provide an updated list of ongoing UCP investigations, similar to the annex to the study5 published in 2020.
How it will ensure that the revision of passenger rights delivers concrete and enforceable improvements for EU travellers.
Supporters6
answer: 1. In 2023 the Commission looked in detail at the rise of air fare prices at that time to better understand the industry dynamics that led to higher prices. No formal investigations were launched.

The analysis has fed into the review (1) of Regulation (EC) No 1008/2008 (2), which is looking inter alia at issues in relation to how to effectively deliver sustainable and affordable air connectivity for all of Europe, while retaining the global competitiveness of EU carriers. 2.

The study referred to by the Honourable Members with the annex containing decisions of national competition authorities was published by the Directorate-General for Internal Policies of the European Parliament. The Commission does not collate and publish the decisions of national competition authorities. 3. In 2013 the Commission proposed a revision of Regulation (EC) No 261/2004 on air passenger rights.

This text was complemented by a legislative proposal (3) in 2023 on enforcement mechanisms, with a view to improving the rules for obtaining reimbursement and compensation for air passengers. Both proposals are now being discussed by the co-legislators. The Commission will continue to support both institutions in order to find a balanced agreement.
